steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported, making them available for use in the custom pagination hook.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building React hooks with state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but ensure you've imported both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Define the PaginationState interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named PaginationState with the following properties: currentPage (number), totalPages (number), pageSize (number), and totalItems (number).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and useState here

// Define the PaginationState interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a properly typed interface that describes the shape of pagination state data.
successCriteria: The PaginationState interface is defined with all four required properties and correct type annotations.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the PaginationState interface with all required properties and proper TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the interface is missing some required properties or has incorrect type annotations. Check that you have currentPage, totalPages, pageSize, and totalItems, all typed as numbers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition doesn't match the requirements. Make sure to define an interface named PaginationState with the four specified properties, all typed as numbers.

steps.title: Define the PaginationOptions interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named PaginationOptions with three required properties: initialPage (number), pageSize (number), and totalItems (number).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.expectedOutcome: A PaginationOptions interface is defined with the correct properties and types.
successCriteria: The PaginationOptions interface exists with initialPage: number, pageSize: number, and totalItems: number properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the PaginationOptions interface with all required properties and proper type annotations.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined an interface, but check that it has all three required properties (initialPage, pageSize, totalItems) with the correct number types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The PaginationOptions interface is missing or incorrect. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword and define all three properties with number types.

steps.title: Create the usePagination hook function
steps.instruction: Create a function called usePagination that accepts a parameter named options of type PaginationOptions and returns a value of type PaginationState.
steps.hint: Define a function with the name usePagination, specify its parameter with the correct type, and declare its return type.
steps.expectedOutcome: A usePagination function is defined with proper TypeScript parameter and return type annotations.
successCriteria: The code contains a function named usePagination that takes an options parameter of type PaginationOptions and declares a return type of PaginationState.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly defined the typed usePagination hook function with proper parameter and return types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function is named usePagination, accepts an options parameter with type PaginationOptions, and specifies a return type of PaginationState.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function definition is missing or incorrect. Create a function named usePagination that accepts options: PaginationOptions and returns PaginationState.

steps.title: Initialize pagination state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside the usePagination function, call useState to initialize pagination state with initial values derived from the options parameter.
steps.hint: Use useState with an initial state object that matches the PaginationState interface, using values from the options parameter.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing state with useState
const [state, setState] = useState({ count: 0, name: 'initial' });
steps.expectedOutcome: The usePagination function will have a useState call that creates pagination state with initial values from options.
successCriteria: useState is called inside usePagination with an initial state object containing currentPage, pageSize, and totalItems derived from options.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the pagination state using useState with values from the options parameter.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling useState with an object that has currentPage, pageSize, and totalItems properties, using values from the options parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside usePagination, you need to call useState to create state with initial values from the options parameter.

steps.title: Calculate totalPages in the state
steps.instruction: Inside the usePagination hook, calculate totalPages by dividing totalItems by pageSize and rounding up using Math.ceil, then include it in the state object returned from useState.
steps.hint: Use Math.ceil(totalItems / pageSize) to get the total number of pages. Add this calculation to your state initialization.
steps.expectedOutcome: The pagination state now includes a totalPages property calculated from totalItems and pageSize.
successCriteria: The useState initialization includes a totalPages property calculated with Math.ceil(totalItems / pageSize).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully calculated the total number of pages based on the items and page size.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include totalPages in the state object and use Math.ceil for proper rounding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The calculation isn't quite right. Remember to divide totalItems by pageSize and round up using Math.ceil, then include it in the state.

steps.title: Create the goToPage handler
steps.instruction: Inside the usePagination hook, define a goToPage function that accepts a page number parameter and updates the paginationState if the page is within valid bounds (1 to totalPages).
steps.hint: Create a function that takes a page number, checks if it's between 1 and totalPages, then calls setPaginationState with the new currentPage.
steps.expectedOutcome: The hook now contains a typed goToPage handler function that validates page numbers before updating state.
successCriteria: A goToPage function is defined that accepts a page number parameter, validates it's within 1 to totalPages, and calls setPaginationState with the updated currentPage.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a typed goToPage handler that validates page numbers before updating the pagination state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a goToPage function, but make sure it validates the page number is between 1 and totalPages before updating state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The goToPage handler is missing or doesn't properly validate page numbers and update the pagination state.

steps.title: Create the nextPage and prevPage handlers
steps.instruction: Inside the usePagination hook, define a nextPage function that calls goToPage with currentPage + 1, and a prevPage function that calls goToPage with currentPage - 1.
steps.hint: Both functions should be defined inside the hook and should use the existing goToPage handler to change pages.
steps.expectedOutcome: The usePagination hook now includes nextPage and prevPage functions that will handle moving to the next and previous pages.
successCriteria: The nextPage and prevPage functions are defined inside the hook and call goToPage with the appropriate page numbers.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the convenience handlers for pagination navigation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined one of the handlers, but both nextPage and prevPage are needed.
steps.feedbackWrong: The nextPage and prevPage handlers are not correctly defined or missing.

steps.title: Return the hook's API
steps.instruction: Return an object from the usePagination hook containing the pagination state and all handler functions (goToPage, nextPage, prevPage).
steps.hint: At the end of your hook function, use the return keyword followed by an object with the state and handlers as properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The hook now returns an object with paginationState, totalPages, goToPage, nextPage, and prevPage, making these values available to components that use the hook.
successCriteria: The usePagination hook returns an object containing paginationState, totalPages, goToPage, nextPage, and prevPage.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully returned the hook's API, making all pagination state and handlers available to consuming components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure you're returning an object with all required properties: paginationState, totalPages, goToPage, nextPage, and prevPage.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook should return an object containing the pagination state and handler functions. Check that you're using the return keyword with the correct object structure.

steps.title: Export the usePagination hook
steps.instruction: Export the usePagination function as the default export so it can be imported in other components.
steps.hint: Add the export statement at the end of the file, after the function definition.
steps.expectedOutcome: The usePagination hook is exported and ready to be used in other TypeScript components.
successCriteria: The usePagination function is exported as the default export.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the usePagination hook. It's now available for import in other components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the correct export syntax for default exports.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook isn't exported correctly. Remember to use 'export default usePagination' at the end of the file.
